title: Americans' Thanksgiving Dinner Is Getting More Expensive
paragraphs: From delectable roast turkey to cranberry sauce and sweet potatoes, Thanksgiving in the US wouldn't be complete without a hearty meal shared with family and friends.
But putting that meal on the table is putting a bigger hole in people's wallets.
The American Farm Bureau Federation's annual Thanksgiving dinner survey found that a meal for 10 people costs about $59 this year. That's an increase of more than 6% from 2025.
This is the first time since 2022 that the survey has recorded an increase in the cost of a Thanksgiving dinner.
The price of turkey has seen one of the biggest increases. A frozen turkey weighing about 7.3 kilograms now costs an average of about $24, an increase of 10% from last year.
The cost of cranberries has increased by nearly 9%. Other ingredients like milk, bread rolls, stuffing mix and sweet potatoes have also increased in price.
The Farm Bureau said high fuel prices and a shortage of farm workers have affected food production costs.

However, not everything has become more expensive. Frozen peas, frozen pie crusts and whipping cream all cost less than they did last year. That's good news for people who like pumpkin pie, a classic Thanksgiving dessert.
The survey also shows how Thanksgiving meal prices have changed over time.
In 2020, a dinner for 10 cost just under $47. Prices reached a record high of more than $64 in 2022 before falling again in subsequent years.
So although it's more expensive this year than it was last year, the cost of a Thanksgiving dinner is actually still 8% lower than it was four years ago.
American Thanksgiving is held on the fourth Thursday in November. This year, that makes it November 26.

The Thanksgiving dinner survey has been done every year since 1986. Hundreds of volunteer shoppers across all 50 US states and Puerto Rico take part by checking the prices of ingredients at local grocery stores.
